validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today's Microsoft Build 2026 keynote lands the originating evidence for the prediction. Satya Nadella opened at Fort Mason this morning with an in-house MAI model family debuting on stage, including a coding-focused model explicitly positioned to power GitHub Copilot — Microsoft's most direct move yet to reduce foundation-model dependence on OpenAI. The day-prior June 1 GitHub Copilot switch to usage-based billing is the other half of the same margin story: premium request units gave way to per-token GitHub AI Credits, and the fallback that let users who exhausted an allowance drop to a cheaper model and keep working was removed, so metered billing now exposes Microsoft's own gross margin on every agentic Copilot request. The Build framing pitches the first-party MAI coding model as the lower-inference-cost engine under the new metered plans, and the autonomous GitHub Copilot pushed from pair programmer toward an agent assigned bugs, features, and pull requests is exactly the high-volume agentic path where a model Microsoft does not pay OpenAI per-token for is the cleanest lever. What has not yet printed is the Copilot release-note language naming a first-party model as the default for completions or agent mode, or distinct per-model token rates in the published GitHub AI Credits table.

prediction_ref.short_label: BadHost CVE-2026-48710 CVSS score gets upgraded above 6.5 by Q4 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today's fresh BadHost analysis lands the originating evidence for the prediction. BadHost (CVE-2026-48710) is a host-header injection flaw in the Starlette ASGI framework — the routing core under FastAPI — that lets an attacker control the path a request appears to target by inserting a single character into the HTTP Host header, defeating any path-based authentication middleware. Starlette pulls roughly 325 million downloads a week, and the affected surface reaches directly into the local-LLM serving stack: FastAPI, vLLM, LiteLLM, and MCP servers whose spec mandates unauthenticated OAuth discovery endpoints, with researchers chaining the primitive to authentication bypass, server-side request forgery, and in some cases remote code execution. The disclosing researchers at X41 D-Sec, who found it during an OSTIF-sponsored vLLM audit, have already gone on record that the assigned CVSS 6.5 understates the downstream impact given how cleanly the single-character primitive escalates. That combination of mass deployment and clean escalation is the profile that drives post-disclosure score inflation as exploitation paths get demonstrated and vendors shipping affected gateways issue advisories above the conservative initial rating. The fix shipped in Starlette 1.0.1 on May 21. Not yet printed: an NVD re-score of the record or a downstream vendor advisory rating the flaw high severity.
